subject: MedForge POC environment activation & gating plan
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Sun <claire@medforge.com>, MedForge POC <poc@medforge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MedForge POC environment activation & gating plan

Claire / MedForge team —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. To keep momentum toward the POC close window, I've attached a concise playbook and a network allowlist template that capture the MAP items we discussed. This email lays out our recommended, minimum gating sequence so your infra and security teams can review quickly. High-level asks:

- Org & billing seed: create a MedForge Redwood org (we can accept SSO later) — we need an admin contact and tenant ID for provisioning.
- API keys: production-like API key (ephemeral/service-account pattern) issuance for POC traffic.
- IP allowlist: CIDRs for traffic to Redwood hosted endpoints (template attached).
- VPC peering: optional/strongly recommended for lowest latency and data isolation — confirm if you want a peering or prefer routed ingress.

Target timeline (proposal):
- API keys provisioned by Tue, 2028-03-06
- IP allowlist entries accepted by Wed, 2028-03-07
- VPC peering window (if needed): Fri–Sat, 2028-03-09/10

Please review the attached MAP_Playbook_MedForge_v1.pdf and the Network_Allowlist_Template.csv. If your security team needs a one-pager with SOC / audit artifacts, Jordan can attach that. Can you confirm: 1) the infra/security point-of-contact for the peering window and 2) whether MedForge will require a Private VPC peering or is OK with IP allowlisting to start?

Thanks — once we have the two confirmations above we'll lock the MAP timeline and create the HubSpot mutual action plan card.

– Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success (POC & Trials)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Playbook_MedForge_v1.pdf (doc), Network_Allowlist_Template.csv (csv)

- Infra contact for peering/window: Mateo Lin (mateo.lin@medforge.com) — looping him in separately from our side.
- Security review: we're handing the MAP_Playbook to our InfoSec team; they asked for the Redwood SOC-2 summary and a short note on key rotation (Jordan, can you add that?).
- VPC peering: initial preference is to start with IP allowlisting so we can begin tests earlier; we may request peering before full-scale evaluation.

Attached is a vCard for our infra owner.

We'll aim to have the CIDR(s) to you by Tues (3/6) EOD. If anything slips on our end we'll call it out immediately.

Claire
Claire Sun

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Mar 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedForge POC environment activation & gating plan — technical notes

Hi all — couple of technical clarifications/from the engineering side to keep the gating unambiguous: 

1) API keys & service accounts:
   - For the POC we recommend creating a scoped service-account API key (read/write tokens limited to the POC tenant). We'll rotate keys at 48h intervals during stress runs.
   - If MedForge prefers ephemeral keys, we can issue a short-lived token exchange flow; that requires a callback URL and a service principal.

2) IP allowlist specifics:
   - We accept CIDR ranges for both egress to API endpoints and a fallback allowlist for our streaming worker IPs. Please use the Network_Allowlist_Template.csv and include both /32 addresses for NAT and broader /24 where org policy requires.

3) VPC peering options:
   - Option A (recommended): Regional VPC peering between your VPC and our dedicated POC VPC — fastest, lower egress complexity. Needs an agreed maintenance window for route table updates (we suggested 3/9–3/10).
   - Option B: Continue with allowlist & TLS over public endpoints; lower engineering overhead but may add ~40–80ms tail latency.

Proposed concrete milestones to land the MAP before the end of next week: 
- 2028-03-06: MedForge provides tenant ID + primary admin and CIDR(s) (we'll provision API key stub).
- 2028-03-07: Redwood confirms allowlist acceptance and issues full API key.
- 2028-03-09: Optional peering window (if MedForge selects Option A).

I'll drop a short tech checklist into the shared Drive (link below) — please fill the CIDRs and preferred peering option in the sheet so Neha can schedule firewall changes.

Tech checklist link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-MedForge-POC

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: MAP snapshot & updated mutual timeline — please confirm

Claire / Team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on Claire's note and Jordan's checklist, I've formalized the MAP snapshot and attached a simple CSV timeline (MAP_Timeline_v1.csv) so it's easy to import into your ticketing system. Summary below — please confirm or flag changes by EOD Wed, 2028-03-07: 

Mutual action plan highlights:
- Tenant + Admin contact provided: MedForge -> Mateo Lin
- API keys: Redwood to issue scoped POC key upon receipt of tenant ID (target 2028-03-06)
- IP allowlist: MedForge to provide CIDR(s) by 2028-03-06 EOD; Redwood to confirm acceptance by 2028-03-07
- Peering: default = allowlist for initial tests; optional peering on 2028-03-09/10 if MedForge requests tighter isolation

Risks & contingencies:
- If InfoSec requests additional artifacts, Jordan will send SOC and key-rotation notes (Jordan — can you attach the SOC-2 summary to the HubSpot card?).
- If CIDR provisioning misses the 3/6 window, we'll still provision an ephemeral test key but schedule full-load testing the week after.

Next steps (action owners):
- Claire / Mateo: confirm CIDR(s and preferred peering option) — action by 2028-03-06 EOD
- Jordan / Neha: prepare firewall change window & test plan once CIDRs are in the sheet
- Grace: create HubSpot MAP card and set the mutual close target to 2028-03-15 (adjustable)

I'll consider this plan accepted once I get a one-line confirmation from Claire or Mateo. Thanks — excited to get the POC live.

Best,
Grace
